title: Grateful Dead Live at Carousel Ballroom on 1968-03-29
lineage: Dat (Sony R500) -> Adobe Audition v3.0 -> Samplitude Professional v11.03 -> FLAC

ai_review.summary: Superb early‑68 Carousel Ballroom show with a smoking New Potato Caboose and soaring Dark Star, captured in an open‑feel matrix recording that sounds crystal clear.
ai_review.review: The March 29 1968 performance is hailed as one of the band’s most swinging early shows – standout moments include a sublime New Potato Caboose solo by Jerry, a powerful Death Don't Have No Mercy and an exploratory Dark Star.  Charlie Miller’s matrix transfer delivers exceptional clarity with stage‑mic ambience, only punctuated by occasional crowd chatter.

ai_rating.rationale: The majority of reviews (13) are 5‑star and praise both the musical performance and the audio quality; only a few low‑rating comments note minor audience‑type artifacts, leading to an overall rating well above 4.5.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Early soundboard/stage‑mic matrix with crystal‑clear instrument separation; occasional hall echo and crowd chatter are audible but do not detract from the overall superior clarity.

show_quality.setlist_flow: A swinging, high‑energy set that feels like the early ’68 carousel shows; an announcer appears after Morning Dew suggesting a brief break or possible two‑set structure.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia’s solo on New Potato Caboose is described as sublime and one of his best ever; he also explores Dark Star with adventurous improvisation.
band_member_comments.Bob: Good Morning Little School Girl highlighted for its tasty vocal delivery; Bob’s (or Ron’s) vocal moments are praised.
band_member_comments.Keys: Keyboard/organ sounds are noted as crystal clear on Dark Star and a mournful tone on Death Don't Have No Mercy; Pigpen’s organ cursing is audible in one segment.
